relationships.subject: CeA PKCδ neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Inhibition of CeA-PKCδ or CeA-CGRPR neurons significantly mitigated tactile hypersensitivity at both the acute and chronic phases, but the effects were much more pronounced at the acute phase

relationships.subject: PB-CeA pathway
relationships.evidence_quote: Accordingly, chemogenetic inhibition of the PB→CeA pathway mitigated pain-related behaviors in acute, but not chronic, neuropathic pain.

key_findings: PB-CeA synaptic plasticity and CRF neuron hyperexcitability occur in acute but not chronic neuropathic pain.
Non-CRF neurons, including a SOM subset, become hyperexcitable at the chronic phase.
